newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down on Tuesday on profit-taking from retail investors, but an upward trend was likely in the long term, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,328 yuan ($401) per tonne, losing seven yuan. It opened at 3,330 yuan and hit a high of 3,336 yuan per tonne.
March fell 31 to 3,180, May did not trade, July fell 60 to 3,370, November seven to 3,338 and the January 1998 contract six to 3,346.
Combined volume fell to 23,300 tonnes from 23,700.
"Profit-taking pushed all contracts down to end at their intraday lows," one trader said.
"But many investors believed the day's fall was a technical correction following heavy gains in the past few days," he added.
Traders said soybeans had the potential to rise further in the long term as fundamentals were improving.
"The recent continuous rises in spot soybeans prices will support futures contracts," a second trader said.
